cells.tense: Right now you are the one holding what you set out to make, and you know it is yours.
cells.ask: Name the one direction you'd keep if everything else went, say it once out loud, and let that be the answer
cells.core:
You made a call at some point, and the thing you called for is real now — sitting in front of you, finished enough to be judged. Not a possibility anymore. That's why it takes directing rather than imagining; it only moves if you decide where it goes next.

The pull right now is to keep choosing out of what you've already built, and that's steady. It's also narrow — finished work tends to steer you into more of the same shape. Keep one thing in view that has nothing to do with what you finished, and let it be allowed to pull, even if it goes nowhere yet. Deciding stays yours; it just doesn't have to be decided by the last thing.
cells.sheetLine: Finished work can steer you into more of the same shape.
cells.place: where direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You are already living past the point where this finishes, and the present keeps catching you off guard.
cells.ask: Stop one thing mid-step today, look at what is actually in front of you before working out what it means
cells.core:
You're pushing this to an end that hasn't happened yet — planning the next version, working out how it will land, deciding what it will prove. Every step gets measured against a finish line you keep moving. From outside it looks like ambition; from where you sit it's bracing, and the bracing is the tell.

What you're missing is the plain look at a thing before you've decided what it is. You keep determining where this goes because you've already determined it. Try one thing you can't be right about yet and leave it unnamed for an hour. The direction stays yours either way. The pressure is the part that isn't.
cells.sheetLine: Deciding where this goes is not the same as being right about it.

cells.tense: Something got finished behind you, and you are still standing at the door it closed.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually made, plainly, no undercutting it, and stop talking when you're done
cells.core:
You carried something to its end and then stopped short of the part where it counts as yours. The last stretch may have been long. Either way you're not quite in the room with what you finished — you describe it, you keep it moving, you don't land in it.

Direction will come back, but not from deciding harder. It comes from letting something reach you: a moment, a word from someone, your own body in a chair. Let one thing land today without doing anything to it. You can finish a thing. Being here while it finishes is the part to pick up now.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it and stopped short of landing in it.

cells.tense: You are already steering where this goes, and you talk about it like it steers itself.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made this week and say it was yours, without waiting for it to feel settled
cells.core:
You keep saying the work went this way, or the situation called for it, or things just landed there. But somebody decided. Somebody chose the version that got made, and it was you — it shows in how fluently you can explain the choices afterward.

Working, this is a person holding a finished thing and saying plainly that they chose to make it. Not boastful and not apologizing, just the fact of it, with whatever comes next riding on top. The direction is running whether or not you claim it. What's missing is the moment where you say this was mine. Not the whole thing — one choice. It doesn't have to be a finished thought. Anyone can watch you hold a thing you made and call it yours.
cells.sheetLine: Somebody decided. You can hear it in how you explain it.

Reader could reasonably say 'I'm not weighed down, it's just finished'; the cells therefore stay on the question of what to do with what exists, and the ask stands even if the reading is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line congratulating the person on having finished something — dropped.
